PNEUMONIA
Introduction
An inflammation of the lung parenchyma
Various bacterial species, fungi and viruses may cause pneumonia
The setting in which infection is acquired could be a predictor of the infecting
pathogen
Bacterial Pneumonia: is defined as bacterial infection of the lung parenchyma
associated with recently developed radiological shadowing which may be
segmental, lobar or multi lobar.
Types
- Community Acquired Pneumonia (CAP)
- Hospital Acquired pneumonia (HAP)
- Ventilator Associated pneumonia (VAP)
- Health care associated Pneumonia (HCAP)
- Pneumonia in the immunocompromised
- Aspiration pneumonia

Common bacteria causing CAP:
- Streptococcus pneumonia(Most common cause)
- Mycoplasma pneumonia
- Legionella pneumophilia
- Chlamydia pneumonia
- Haemophilus influenza
- Staphylococcus aureus
- Chlamydia psittaci
- Coxiella burnetti
- Klebsiella pneumonia
- Actinomyces israelli
- Haemophilus influenzae
- Pseudomonas aeruginosa (usually implicated in nosocomial pneumonia)
